tagline: Ranch country and the Snake River canyon, some 150 miles.
intro: Out of Baker City the byway goes through rangeland to Richland, a town of about 165. From there Snake River Road runs high above Brownlee Reservoir and down to Huntington, and the way back toward Baker City comes through Rye Valley. It is about 150 miles of paved, gravel and dirt road, and near the Oregon Trail interpretive center outside Baker City the old wagon ruts are kept where they lie.
The draws along the canyon were good country for hiding. Outlaws rowed across to cabins on the Idaho side, and the moonshiners were left alone, since the locals did not count it a crime.

moments.title: Snake River Road
moments.text: High above Brownlee Reservoir the road runs under big outcrops of many-colored basalt, until it comes down to the water and the rock turns metamorphic and sedimentary for the last miles to Huntington.

moments.title: Huntington
moments.text: A stagecoach station that became a railroad division point in 1884, and by the century's end a town known as Sin City, until Governor Oswald West set out to clean it up.

moments.title: Rye Valley
moments.text: A settlement on Dixie Creek named for the native grass that fed the pack animals of the 1860s miners and emigrants, with a post office that came and went until 1935.

practical: The byway mixes paved, gravel and dirt roads suited to high-clearance two-wheel-drive vehicles, and the BLM advises care after bad weather and in winter.
